answer: Divergent history checks. Each identity maintains a signed event thread; on first contact, peers exchange a random comet challenge and require the two histories to share a common vertex within the last N events. A clone can copy a history only by freezing it, so any fork is detectable and both branches get rejected. Creating k usable identities costs the attacker k separate live histories kept current with real interactions, roughly k times the ongoing work of one honest agent.
